title: Israeli Couscous with Tabcha Spinach, White Wine and Butter
subtitle: in a sage and garlic white wine sauce
description: Israeli couscous is blanched and tossed in a reduced white wine, sage and garlic sauce enriched with butter and slow-cooked crispy spinach (tabcha). In the restaurant it comes with eggplant schnitzel.

steps.text: For the tabcha, heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot, add the spinach and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until it shrinks. Add the remaining oil and cook for 3 hours over low heat until the spinach is crisp and turns black.
For the sauce, heat the olive oil in a pot and fry the sliced garlic and sage for about 1 minute until the garlic is lightly golden. Add the wine and cook for about 20 minutes until reduced by half.
Add the water, 3 tbsp of the tabcha and the butter, season with salt and pepper and stir well until the butter melts into the sauce. Remove from the heat.
Blanch the Israeli couscous in plenty of boiling salted water for 4 minutes, then transfer to iced water and drain.
Add the couscous to the pot with the sauce, stir and leave for 5 minutes to absorb the flavours.
